chapter.name: Universal Franchise and India's Electoral System
chapter.blurb: Theme D, Governance and Democracy: what universal adult franchise means, the scale of Indian elections and the measures that make voting accessible, a school election caselet on the secret ballot and NOTA, the Election Commission of India, polling day with the EVM and VVPAT, the Model Code of Conduct, and direct and indirect elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha and the offices of President and Vice President.

scope_in.item: State what universal adult franchise means: one vote for every citizen aged 18 and above, all votes of equal value, irrespective of caste, creed, race, religion, gender, education or income
Use the terms franchise, suffrage, constituency and system as the chapter defines them in its margins
Name Article 326 as the constitutional basis, and list the elections it covers: Lok Sabha, the legislative assembly of every state and union territory, and all local elections in villages and cities
Apply the two limits the chapter states: a voter must be registered in her own constituency, no one may vote on another's behalf, and a person guilty of certain serious crimes is barred

Recall that the voting age was lowered from 21 to 18 in 1988, that about 13 per cent of Indians could vote before Independence, and that Indian women had the vote from the beginning while Swiss women got it only in 1971

Explain, from the chapter's mindmap, why universal adult franchise matters: power to determine one's future, equality, every voice counting, representatives answerable to the electorate and civic engagement

Quote the scale of Indian elections: over 968 million eligible voters and 543 Lok Sabha constituencies in 2024, over 1 million polling stations, and 3.1 million elected representatives (1.3 million of them women) in more than 250,000 local bodies
Explain why scale and diversity make Indian elections hard to run: the electorate is fifteen times the population of the United Kingdom and the country six times the area of France

List the accessibility measures the Election Commission used so no voter is left behind: officials travelling to remote locations, home voting for the elderly and persons with disabilities in 2024, postal voting for a specific category, braille-enabled voter cards and app-based requests for wheelchairs and ramps
State that about 34 per cent of eligible voters did not vote in 2024, and suggest reasons and remedies
Describe the 10th-century Uttaramerur process of selecting representatives by palm-leaf fragments drawn from a sealed pot in public

Retell the Suryodaya School class representative caselet: the candidates and their promises, campaigning, the Election Officer, the secret ballot, the braille ballot, the sealed box, the witness at the count, the invalid ballot and the result
Explain what NOTA is, that India offers it, and that it does not change the result but signals that voters want better choices

Describe the Election Commission of India as an independent constitutional body set up in 1950, conducting elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and the offices of President and Vice President, with the first general elections held in 1951-1952

Name the levels and officers in the Election Commission's structure: Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners at national level, Chief Electoral Officer at state or union territory level, District Election Officer, Returning Officer who conducts the election and Electoral Registration Officer who manages the voter list
List the Election Commission's tasks: setting election dates, enforcing the Model Code of Conduct, registering political parties and overseeing the entire electoral process
State that State Election Commissions manage direct elections to gram panchayats and urban local bodies, in consultation with the Election Commission of India
State that elections happen at different times with some periodicity, so polls fall due in various parts of the country every year, and that many people including teachers are deployed
Recall that 84 Lok Sabha constituencies are reserved for scheduled castes and 47 for scheduled tribes, leaving 412 general

Describe the four steps of voting at a polling station: name and ID checked, finger inked and signature taken, chit taken and finger checked with NOTA available, and the EVM button pressed with a beep and a VVPAT slip
Explain what a VVPAT does and why a paper record matters, and recall that Namibia and Bhutan have used Indian EVMs and VVPAT with Election Commission support
Recall Shyam Saran Negi, a school teacher in Himachal Pradesh, as the first voter in the 1951 general elections, voting again in 2017 at the age of 100

State the purpose and three listed elements of the Model Code of Conduct, and identify breaches of the kind the chapter illustrates: gifts to voters, abusive language, government officials campaigning for the ruling party and cash carried by a candidate
Recall the history of the Model Code of Conduct: adopted in Kerala in 1960, circulated by the Election Commission during the 1962 general elections, and enforced proactively from 1991
Recall T.N. Seshan as Chief Election Commissioner from 1990 and his reforms: precise campaigning rules, voter IDs to end proxy voting and strict vigilance on candidate spending
Explain the First-Past-the-Post system: the candidate with the most votes in a constituency wins, even without half the votes, as Gurmat won with 12 of 33
Distinguish an MP from an MLA and name the regional words for the legislative assembly, such as Vidhan Sabha and Niyama Sabha

Describe government formation: the party or coalition with a majority of Lok Sabha seats forms the national government and its leader usually becomes prime minister, and the same at state level for the chief minister

Explain indirect election using the school council analogy, and describe the Rajya Sabha: 245 members, 233 elected by MLAs and 12 nominated by the President, seats allotted by state population, a permanent house never dissolved, six-year terms with one-third retiring every two years, elected by single transferable vote

Describe the electoral college that elects the President: elected members of both Houses of Parliament and MLAs of the states and of Delhi and Puducherry, voting by single transferable vote, and name the four groups excluded and the reason for excluding them

Describe the election of the Vice President by an electoral college of the elected and nominated members of both Houses of Parliament, and name his role as chairperson of the Rajya Sabha who steps in for the President
Name the three challenges the chapter lists, the influence of money, candidates with criminal records and voter apathy especially in urban areas, and the road ahead of an informed and vigilant voter

concepts.name: Universal adult franchise: meaning, reach and history
concepts.description: What universal adult franchise means, the constitutional basis in Article 326, the conditions and limits on the right to vote, and how India came to adopt it.
concepts.idea: Every Indian citizen aged 18 and above gets one vote, and every vote counts the same.
concepts.rule: Franchise means a right granted by the constitution or government; suffrage is a synonym. Universal adult franchise means every citizen aged 18 and above has the right to vote irrespective of caste, creed, race, religion, gender, education or income, and every vote has equal value. Article 326 of the Constitution makes elections to the Lok Sabha, to the legislative assembly of every state and union territory, and all local elections in villages and cities rest on universal franchise. A voter must be registered in her own constituency, no one may vote on another's behalf, and a person found guilty of certain serious crimes is barred from voting. India adopted universal adult franchise from the outset and lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 in 1988.
concepts.example: A seventeen-year-old cannot vote, but once she turns 18 and registers, her single vote counts exactly as much as a minister's.

concepts.idea: India trusted every adult with the vote from the very beginning, when few countries did.

concepts.name: Scale, diversity and bridging barriers to voting
concepts.description: The size and diversity of India's electorate, and the measures the Election Commission takes so that no voter is left behind.
concepts.idea: An election is free and fair only if every eligible voter is actually able to cast her vote.
concepts.rule: Over 968 million voters were eligible in the 2024 general election, for the 543 constituencies of the Lok Sabha. Postal voting was available for a specific category of voters. Assistive measures include braille-enabled voter cards and app-based requests for help such as wheelchairs and ramps. Even so, about 34 per cent of eligible voters did not vote in 2024.

concepts.idea: An independent body outside the government of the day runs India's elections.
concepts.rule: The Election Commission of India is an independent constitutional body responsible for conducting free and fair elections. It was established in 1950 and conducts elections to the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha, the State Legislative Assemblies and the offices of the President and the Vice President. The first general elections in independent India were held in 1951-1952. At the national level it has a Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners; at state and union territory level a Chief Electoral Officer; at district level a District Election Officer, a Returning Officer who conducts the election and an Electoral Registration Officer who manages the voter list. Its tasks include setting election dates, enforcing the Model Code of Conduct, registering political parties and overseeing the entire electoral process. Elections to gram panchayats and urban local bodies are managed by the State Election Commissions, working in consultation with the Election Commission of India.

concepts.name: Direct elections: Lok Sabha, assemblies and First-Past-the-Post
concepts.description: How voters directly elect MPs and MLAs, what the First-Past-the-Post system means, and how a government is formed after the results.
concepts.idea: In each constituency the candidate with the most votes wins, and the party or coalition with most seats forms the government.
concepts.rule: India is divided into 543 constituencies for the Lok Sabha. Those elected to the Lok Sabha are Members of Parliament, or MPs; those elected to a state assembly are Members of Legislative Assembly, or MLAs, and the assembly is called Vidhan Sabha or Niyama Sabha in some regional languages. India uses the First-Past-the-Post system, in which the candidate receiving the most votes in a constituency wins, so a candidate can win without securing even 50 per cent of the votes. After the results, the party or coalition winning a majority of the seats in the Lok Sabha forms the national government and its leader typically becomes the prime minister; at state level the leader of the majority becomes the chief minister. concepts.name: Indirect elections and the road ahead
concepts.description: How the Rajya Sabha, the President and the Vice President are elected indirectly, and the challenges the chapter names for India's electoral system.
concepts.idea: Some offices are filled not by voters directly but by the representatives whom voters have already elected.
concepts.rule: In an indirect election, representatives who were themselves elected choose the next set of representatives, as a school council chosen by class representatives would be. Of the Rajya Sabha's 245 members, 233 are elected by the elected members of the state legislative assemblies and 12 are nominated by the President. Seats are allotted to states by population, so Uttar Pradesh has more than Arunachal Pradesh. The Rajya Sabha is the Permanent House and is never dissolved; a member's term is six years and one-third of the members retire every two years. Voting uses the single transferable vote system, which helps smaller states get fair representation. The President is elected by an electoral college of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the MLAs of the states and of Delhi and Puducherry, by single transferable vote; nominated members of the Rajya Sabha and of state assemblies, members of Legislative Councils and nominated members of Delhi and Puducherry are left out, so that only directly elected representatives choose the President. The Vice President is elected by an electoral college of the elected and nominated members of both Houses of Parliament, and is chairperson of the Rajya Sabha. The challenges named are the growing influence of money, candidates with criminal records and voter apathy, especially in urban areas.
